title: Agent and CLI contract: who writes which file
ask: Do agents call the CLI, or edit files themselves?
why: Decides whether state stays valid when several agents and people touch the same files. Replaces F2d.
learn: lc-wms verbs and validator hook; control-center verbs.toml; deepseek-harness approval design
rec_reason: Split by file type. Prose (markdown) is what agents are good at editing, so they edit it directly. State (TOML, JSONL) is where mistakes corrupt things, so only the CLI writes it. This also keeps token cost down: the agent asks for a digest instead of reading files. Paperclip itself warns that installed MCP apps load their tools into context on every run, while permitted-only tools add no context cost; a CLI costs nothing until it is called. Also verify after writing: Paperclip had a run whose status write failed with an empty token and left a ticket in the wrong state until a later run re-read it.

options.label: CLI for all state, direct edits for prose. Agents call the CLI to change TOML and JSONL and to read digests; they edit markdown (spec, plan, notes) themselves. Direct writes to TOML are denied by permission rules and a validator hook checks everything
options.desc: One safe write path for state.

options.must: Decided rule: CLI for all state, direct edits for prose.

options.label: Expose the verbs as an MCP server; agents call typed tools instead of the shell
